defect.evidence_quote: the preference for categorical treatment of Fourth Amendment claims gives way to individualized review when a defendant makes a colorable argument that an arrest, with or without a warrant, was "conducted in an extraordinary manner"
defect.locator_note: text/Atwater v. City of Lago Vista__6ef739.txt lines 83-89; page 354 supports the rule, page 355 applies it.
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the phrase 'probable cause governs all arrests without individualized balancing' is too absolute unless the extraordinary-manner caveat is included.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: A warrantless custodial arrest for a fine-only misdemeanor committed in the officer's presence, supported by probable cause, ordinarily does not violate the Fourth Amendment; absent an arrest conducted in an extraordinary manner unusually harmful to privacy or physical interests, no case-by-case balancing is required.

reasons: Page 354 states that probable cause applies to all arrests without balancing and that an officer with probable cause for even a very minor offense in his presence may arrest without violating the Fourth Amendment.
Page 355 states Turek was authorized to make a custodial arrest without balancing costs and benefits because Atwater admitted the seatbelt offense in his presence.
The opinion also preserves individualized review for extraordinary manner arrests, so the holding field should carry that limitation.
residual_risks: The proposition should not be read to decide home-entry or extraordinary-manner arrest issues beyond Atwater's facts.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the extraordinary-manner caveat directly to the holding field.

reasons: The SIA Persons role is only Related (cross-doctrine), not a claimed SIA holding.
The opinion links custodial arrest to searches of the person through Robinson; the dissent notes that under today's holding an officer may arrest the driver and search the driver.
residual_risks: Atwater itself decides arrest authority, not the scope of search incident to arrest.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep this as Related only; do not promote it to a key SIA authority.

reasons: The case directly addresses whether the Fourth Amendment forbids warrantless arrest for a minor offense committed in the officer's presence.
The text holds that if an officer has probable cause for even a very minor criminal offense in his presence, he may arrest the offender without violating the Fourth Amendment.
residual_risks: The key role should remain limited to minor-offense custodial arrest on probable cause, not broader arrest-warrant doctrine.

reasons: The page and opinion frame the claimed Fourth Amendment injury as an unreasonable seizure of the person.
A full custodial arrest is a person seizure, so a Related cross-doctrine placement is supported.
residual_risks: Atwater is primarily an arrest authority rather than a general seizure taxonomy case.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep as Related rather than Key.
